blocks.text: Cloverdale Acreages: streets and boundaries

items.t: Cloverdale acreage sits on the lowland edges of the Cloverdale community in the City of Surrey: the Serpentine and Nicomekl River lowlands west and south of the town centre, along 176 Street (Highway 15), Colebrook Road and the 64 Avenue corridor.

The City describes Cloverdale's borders as 160 Street to the west and 48 Avenue to the south, with Langley to the east; the acreage pockets lie inside the southern and western lowland part of that frame, not in Clayton's built subdivisions.
Serpentine is a Fraser Valley Real Estate Board sub-area; the cloverdale-farms feed's visible farm listings were Serpentine listings on 176 Street.

blocks.text: Cloverdale Acreages: the housing stock

items.t: The farm zones are confirmed on a City of Surrey bylaw: the Development Cost Charge (DCC) Bylaw No. 21174 zone list names A-1 General Agriculture and A-2 Intensive Agriculture in Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000.

Servicing is parcel by parcel in the lowlands: the City's lowlands system drains farm fields through ditches, flood boxes and pump stations, which is drainage servicing, not proof of municipal water or sewer at a lot line.

blocks.text: Cloverdale Acreages: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) rules govern first on ALR parcels: subdivision needs Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) approval, a principal residence is capped at 500 square metres (m²) without an ALC application with no more than 1,000 m² of fill, a suite is allowed only inside that residence, and one additional residence is capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 hectares (ha) or less or 186 m² over 40 ha.
Streamside setbacks in Surrey are in Part 7A of Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 and vary by stream class, so no single setback figure applies to a Cloverdale acreage crossed by a ditch or creek.

Surrey's sea dams on the Nicomekl and Serpentine Rivers, first built in 1912 and 1913, keep saline water out of farm irrigation water; a lowland parcel's drainage and irrigation both depend on that system, not only on its own ditch.

blocks.text: Cloverdale Acreages: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Without the Serpentine and Nicomekl sea dams and dykes, parts of Cloverdale and Highways 10, 15 and 99 would flood twice daily at high tide, per the City's July 28, 2025 dyking district report.
The sea dams also store fresh water for agricultural irrigation, so the same gates that block salt water are part of a lowland farm's summer water supply.
The lowlands were reclaimed for farming from the late 1800s by dyking and canals, and the Surrey Dyking District was formed in 1910 to build the two sea dams.

Farm neighbours have a working landscape: dredging to maintain dykes and drainage, and flood spillway cells on agricultural fields, are normal operations in the Serpentine lowland, not future development signals.

blocks.text: Cloverdale Acreages: development and new projects

items.t: Serpentine and Nicomekl River Sea Dams replacement, and transfer of the Surrey and Colebrook Dyking Districts: City of Surrey Corporate Report R174, Council date July 28, 2025, sought direction on replacing both sea dams and on the provincial transfer of the dormant dyking districts. Status: direction sought (as of November 3, 2026) (check current).

Serpentine and Nicomekl Lowlands Drainage Servicing Update was presented to the City's Agricultural and Food Policy Committee on March 10, 2026, covering drainage works that service each agricultural property by a pump station, flood box or localized filling. Status: update presented (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Cloverdale Acreages: costs and taxes

items.t: Surrey's 2026 total residential (Class 1) tax rate is 3.42731 per $1,000 of assessed value, made up of a municipal total of 1.84251 plus school, TransLink, Metro Vancouver, BC Assessment and Municipal Finance Authority charges; the Class 9 Farm total on the same schedule is 12.57740 per $1,000, applied to farm-class assessed values.
A Class 1, 8 or 9 parcel in Surrey also pays a $300 capital parcel tax collected with property taxes, and drainage parcel taxes are collected with property taxes.

DCCs are imposed under Surrey Development Cost Charge Bylaw, 2024, No. 21174, payable at subdivision or building permit as that bylaw specifies; an acreage buyer planning a new farm building should price the A-1 or A-2 DCC line from that bylaw's schedule (check current).

blocks.text: Cloverdale Acreages: getting around

items.t: Highway 15 (176 Street) is the acreage corridor itself, linking the lowlands north to Highway 1 and south to the Pacific Highway border crossing; Highway 10 (56 Avenue and Ladner Trunk Road) crosses it at Cloverdale town centre.

TransLink's regional connections map shows Cloverdale and Langley Centre as bus nodes on this side of Surrey, with route 531 among the routes shown; the map names no bus route on the rural lowland roads themselves, so most acreage trips are by car.

blocks.text: Cloverdale Acreages: risks and due diligence

items.t: Start with the City's coastal floodplain page and the parcel's flood construction level: the page describes the system that protects the lowlands, but it does not give a lot-level building elevation.
Check ALR status on the ALC maps by PID or civic address before valuing a second dwelling or a split; the map does not state the City zone or the streamside setback for the parcel.
Check for a spillway cell or drainage statutory right of way on title: lowland flood works can sit on farm fields by design, and a title search shows what a listing does not.
